skill.description: Create and refine high-fidelity UI designs with Stitch MCP, using prompt enhancement, design system synthesis, and asset download workflows.
skill.summary: Guide Stitch MCP workflows for UI generation, design editing, and reusable design system documentation.
skill.author: google-labs-code

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting, UI terminology, and relative documentation links. One medium-risk semantic issue remains: the workflow recommends shell-based downloads of generated HTML and screenshots without explicit validation or confirmation safeguards.

remediation.issue: Asset downloads use curl through a command runner without stated validation rules.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before downloading, restrict URLs to trusted Stitch-provided download URLs, sanitize filenames, and write only under .stitch/designs.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Asset Download Command
semantic_findings.description: The workflow tells agents to download HTML and screenshot URLs to .stitch/designs using curl -o via run_command or similar. Without explicit URL validation, filename sanitization, and user confirmation, this can fetch untrusted remote content and write files into the local project.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction directly combines remote URL downloads, shell execution, and local file writes. The intent is legitimate asset management, but the workflow lacks safety constraints around trusted sources and output paths.

content.value_statement: Design prompts often lack the detail needed for consistent, production-quality UI outputs. This skill turns rough requests into structured Stitch MCP workflows, reusable design system notes, and saved design assets.
actual_capabilities: Enhances vague UI requests into structured prompts with design vocabulary and layout details.
Routes design tasks to text generation, screen editing, or design system synthesis workflows.
Uses Stitch MCP tools to generate new screens from enhanced text prompts.
Analyzes Stitch project screens to create a .stitch/DESIGN.md design system reference.
Downloads generated HTML and screenshot assets into a project design directory.
limitations: Requires access to a configured Stitch MCP server and a valid Stitch project.
Does not implement generated designs as application code by itself.
Generated quality depends on the available project context and Stitch model output.
Asset download steps should be reviewed before writing remote content locally.

use_cases.title: Create a polished landing page concept
use_cases.description: Turn a short product idea into a detailed Stitch prompt and generate a high-fidelity screen.

use_cases.title: Maintain visual consistency across screens
use_cases.description: Capture colors, typography, spacing, and component style rules from existing Stitch screens.

use_cases.title: Refine generated UI with targeted edits
use_cases.description: Improve a screen through focused edit instructions instead of regenerating the entire design.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a simple page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new UI screen.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a desktop landing page for a productivity app. Make it clean, trustworthy, and focused on one primary call to action.

prompt_templates.title: Use an existing design system
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a screen that should match existing project styles.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a pricing page for this Stitch project. Use the existing .stitch/DESIGN.md colors, typography, spacing, and button styles.

prompt_templates.title: Edit a generated screen
prompt_templates.scenario: Refine a specific design without full regeneration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit the current dashboard screen. Keep the layout, but make the cards feel more premium and improve the empty states.

prompt_templates.title: Create design system documentation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for documenting reusable visual rules.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the representative Stitch screens in this project and create a .stitch/DESIGN.md file with color roles, typography rules, component styling, and layout principles.

output_examples.input: Design a landing page for a mountain resort.
output_examples.output: A structured Stitch prompt describing serene luxury, glassmorphism surfaces, full-width hero imagery, premium typography, and clear booking calls to action.

output_examples.input: Create a design system file from my Stitch project.
output: Named color roles with hex values

output_examples.input: Make this screen feel more professional.
output_examples.output: Targeted edit guidance that adjusts spacing, hierarchy, shadows, color contrast, and button treatment while preserving the existing layout.

best_practices: Provide the Stitch projectId and intended device type before generation starts.
Create or update .stitch/DESIGN.md before generating multiple related screens.
Use targeted edit workflows for polish when the base layout is already correct.
anti_patterns: Do not regenerate from scratch for small visual changes or copy adjustments.
Do not download generated assets without checking the source URL and destination path.
Do not use vague prompts when brand tone, platform, or page structure matters.

faq.question: What is Stitch Design for?
faq.answer: It helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code create, edit, and document UI designs through Stitch MCP workflows.

faq.question: Do I need Stitch MCP access?
faq.answer: Yes. The main workflows require Stitch MCP tools and a projectId for generation, editing, or screen analysis.

faq.question: Can it build React components?
faq.answer: No. It produces design prompts, Stitch screens, design documentation, and downloaded assets, not production component code.

faq.question: What is .stitch/DESIGN.md?
faq.answer: It is a local design system reference that records visual themes, colors, typography, component styles, and layout rules.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing screen?
faq.answer: Yes. The edit workflow supports targeted changes to existing Stitch screens when the base structure should remain.

faq.question: Are downloaded assets safe by default?
faq.answer: Downloads should be reviewed. Only trusted Stitch-provided URLs should be saved, and outputs should stay under .stitch/designs.
